outputText:
claim: >-
  Read-only O2 follow-up completed for the seven retained Eclipse Theia files.
  At pinned upstream commit 5358262f7ca40ba9a5e7b514914a18202bd2b7e6,
  this subset demonstrates a container-backed contribution mechanism operated by
  frontend and backend lifecycle hosts. It is not a semantic composition
  compiler: it supplies no inert module-declaration algebra, complete profile,
  explicit dependency graph, portable compatibility family, canonical immutable
  plan, or digest. The transferable result is five bounded host-design lessons,
  not evidence for adopting Theia, expanding Get Modular Core, or claiming
  expert/industry consensus.

authority:
  precedence:
    - >-
      Accepted ADR-0001 through ADR-0008 and ADR-0015, the accepted system
      boundary, and digest-pinned contract artifacts control. The current
      contract, readiness report, fixtures, proposed ADRs, and this review cannot
      override them (gm/research/implementation-readiness/report.md:75-106).
    - >-
      Get Modular owns deterministic compilation of inert declarations and a
      complete profile; hosts own executable loading, authorization, readiness,
      lifecycle, routing, drain, cleanup, and recovery
      (gm/docs/architecture/system-boundary.md:13-15,33-45,60-70).
    - >-
      DI container types, executable discovery, global registries, lifecycle,
      and product/plugin runtime types cannot enter Core
      (gm/AGENTS.md:27-34; gm/docs/decisions/0001-product-neutral-deterministic-module-composition.md:30-48).
    - >-
      Dependency order is graph data, not an activation command; registration,
      filesystem, locale, and implicit first-provider order are invalid
      (gm/docs/decisions/0004-freeze-v1-portable-composition-contract-and-plan-digest.md:57-75,77-111;
      gm/docs/decisions/0006-clarify-v1-compiler-normalization-and-entry-points.md:76-114).
    - >-
      ADR-0015 permits narrowly governed private source but neither starts
      implementation nor accepts unresolved public/runtime semantics
      (gm/docs/decisions/0015-block-publication-surfaces-and-runtime-claims-while-decisions-stay-open.md:64-122).
  disposition: >-
    The readiness report remains NO-GO for starting tracked private Core until
    the owner-start and admission conditions are satisfied, and NO-GO for public,
    runtime-conformant, or self-composed claims
    (gm/research/implementation-readiness/report.md:571-612). This source review
    does not change that disposition or accept a decision.

observedBehavior:
  - lesson: "Separate portable semantic identity from runtime lookup identity."
    observation: >-
      Theia uses Symbols and Inversify ServiceIdentifier values for provider,
      contribution-type, and named-binding identity. Its filter documentation
      warns that constructor names are unreliable after minification
      (contribution-provider.ts:20-27,35-39,93-129;
      contribution-filter.ts:20-23,46-63).
    transfer: >-
      Keep Get Modular's validated ASCII module/capability/implementation/slot
      identities independent from host DI tokens, constructors, and class names.
    nonTransferableRisk: >-
      Symbols, constructor identity, and named container bindings are
      process/runtime-local and cannot replace the accepted serializable identity
      algebra or cross-process plan identity.

  - lesson: "Snapshot membership explicitly, but do not confuse collection with dependency compilation."
    observation: >-
      ContainerBasedContributionProvider lazily collects getAll results, optionally
      walks parent containers, applies one filter registry, caches the resulting
      array, and drops its container reference (contribution-provider.ts:30-65).
    transfer: >-
      A future product host can snapshot authorized participants before a lifecycle
      attempt and avoid membership changing midway through phases.
    nonTransferableRisk: >-
      The cached service array is executable object membership, not inert
      declarations, an explicit provider binding list, compatibility validation,
      reachability, SCC analysis, or canonical graph output.

  - lesson: "Scope and ownership must be explicit at the host boundary."
    observation: >-
      The default root-provider helper walks to the top container. The child-based
      variant warns that retaining a short-lived child can keep its cached graph
      alive and leak memory; it is reserved for intentionally child-scoped services
      (contribution-provider.ts:78-129).
    transfer: >-
      Hosts should document attempt/root/connection scope and ensure cached runtime
      objects cannot extend shorter-lived scopes.
    nonTransferableRisk: >-
      Root/child Inversify scope is container lifecycle policy. It must not become
      Get Modular module scope or a Core-owned container.

  - lesson: "Lifecycle phase semantics and failure policy belong to the host."
    observation: >-
      Frontend runs initialize, configure, command/key/menu startup, and onStart in
      ordered loops, catching and logging individual failures; window unload invokes
      onStop synchronously in contribution order
      (frontend-application.ts:81-104,263-330). Backend initialize/configure use
      Promise.all, onStart iterates sequentially, and hook errors are logged while
      processing continues (backend-application.ts:234-288,294-368).
    transfer: >-
      A host must specify phase barriers, sequential versus parallel dispatch,
      readiness meaning, and whether one participant failure aborts, degrades, or
      permits partial service.
    nonTransferableRisk: >-
      The observed loop/registration order is not portable business semantics, and
      catch-and-continue partial startup is not Get Modular's fail-closed semantic
      validation.

  - lesson: "Shutdown needs idempotence, service-availability ordering, deadlines, and honest cancellation limits."
    observation: >-
      Backend shutdown is guarded against repetition, dispatches contribution stops
      in parallel before unbinding the root container, gives each phase a separate
      5000 ms race, admits that timed-out promises may continue, then exits.
      Synchronous exit fallback abandons returned promises
      (backend-application.ts:378-455).
    transfer: >-
      A future host should keep dependencies usable during cleanup, make shutdown
      idempotent, bound waiting, and distinguish deadline expiry from cancellation.
    nonTransferableRisk: >-
      This proves neither per-module unload nor drain, fencing, rollback, safe retry,
      generation cutover, recovery, or cleanup completion. Those remain product-host
      concerns.

applicability:
  core: >-
    Applicable only as boundary-confirming counterevidence: Theia's container and
    lifecycle machinery belongs outside Get Modular's semantic compiler.
  productHost: >-
    Potentially useful as a checklist for membership snapshots, explicit scopes,
    phase policy, error isolation, and shutdown ordering.
  retainedSubsetLimit: >-
    The subset omits container-module declarations, dependency metadata,
    ContributionFilterRegistry implementation, FrontendApplicationContribution
    definition, tests, package manifests, plugin host, upgrade/rebind machinery,
    authorization, isolation mechanisms, and broader product architecture.
    Therefore it cannot establish Theia-wide ordering guarantees, compatibility,
    isolation, dynamic unload, upgrade safety, or recovery behavior.

benefits:
  - "Closes O2's missing-source prerequisite with source-specific observations."
  - "Reinforces the accepted semantic-compiler versus host/container/lifecycle boundary."
  - "Supplies concrete host failure and scope questions without importing framework types."
  - "Preserves portable explicit ordering and compatibility instead of inheriting ambient container behavior."

failureModes:
  - "Registration/container enumeration order leaks into business behavior."
  - "A cached filtered contribution set becomes stale after host rebinding or policy changes."
  - "Child-container retention extends object lifetime and leaks scoped graphs."
  - "Catch-and-log startup creates a partially initialized application without rollback."
  - "Timeout is misreported as cancellation while late cleanup still touches an unbound container."
  - "Symbols or constructors are mistaken for durable module or capability identity."
  - "Filtering executable instances is mistaken for authorization, compatibility, or isolation."

counterexamples:
  - >-
    Symbols and constructors are reasonable within one JavaScript DI process; their
    rejection here follows Get Modular's cross-realm serialized contract, not a
    general defect in Theia.
  - >-
    Catch-and-continue can be a deliberate availability choice for an extensible
    workbench; it is unsuitable as Core validation semantics but may be valid host
    policy.
  - >-
    Sequential frontend hooks intentionally define product startup phases. This
    does not make their contribution enumeration order a portable dependency order.
  - >-
    Parallel backend stop is coherent because the interface requires independent
    stop hooks; it is not evidence for dependency-aware teardown.

  - "Use service locator, container, mutable registry, or filter registry as Core authority."
  - "Treat registration/getAll order as dependency or ordered-many semantics."
  - "Translate lifecycle hooks into CompositionPlan commands."
  - "Treat runtime filtering as explicit absence, compatibility, authorization, or upgrade policy."
  - "Infer entire-product behavior or expert consensus from four implementation files."
  - "Relabel the historical O2 source-unavailable record as if it had originally succeeded."
  - "Copy upstream code without separate legal and dependency review; this review is not legal advice."

openQuestions:
  - "What ordering, if any, does the omitted binding/module-loading layer guarantee for getAll?"
  - "How are filters ordered, mutated, and invalidated by the omitted registry implementation?"
  - "Do omitted tests cover partial startup, shutdown timeout, late settlement, or container-unbind races?"
  - "What mechanisms outside this subset govern plugin compatibility, authorization, process isolation, rebinding, upgrades, and unload?"
  - "Can frontend onStop return asynchronous work, and if so, what guarantees exist on window unload?"
  - "No retained evidence proves runtime behavior because no Theia code or tests were executed."

confidence:
  sourceLevel: "high for the cited functions and manifest provenance"
  transferability: "moderate; lessons are boundary/checklist guidance"
  entireTheiaProduct: "low and explicitly not claimed"
  consensus: "none; this is one bounded O2 model inspection, not expert agreement"

recommendedDecision: >-
  Retain Get Modular's accepted boundary unchanged and record this as a new
  read-only O2 Theia source-inspection result alongside—not over—the historical
  source-unavailable record. Use the five lessons only in future product-host
  design and qualification. Do not adopt Theia, add Inversify, accept a proposed
  ADR, start Core, or alter the readiness verdict on this evidence.

conditionsToReverse:
  - "Accepted successor authority deliberately expands Get Modular beyond inert deterministic compilation."
  - "A product-owned host requirement demonstrates that a shared lifecycle abstraction is necessary."
  - "A broader pinned Theia corpus, including registrations, filter implementation, tests, compatibility, isolation, upgrades, and unload paths, is inspected and independently executed."
  - "Any adoption proposal separately proves dependency, license, security, portability, ordering, failure, and migration behavior against Get Modular's accepted constraints."
